A1.justification: Both 25-page PDFs describe the same jailbreak-tuning study. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, StrongREJECT evaluations, baseline comparisons, and analyses of poisoning rates, training settings, and attack variants.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds MMLU evaluations of capability retention across four OpenAI models.

M1.justification: The fine-tuning procedure, attack families, and inference-time modifications in Section 4 and Appendix C are unchanged. The new MMLU answer-extraction procedure concerns evaluation, not the proposed attack method.

E1.justification: v2 adds benign general-knowledge evaluation on MMLU across 57 subjects, extending coverage beyond harmful-response evaluation to capability retention. Existing training datasets and harmful-task evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged, including the covert fine-tuning and additional prompt-based attacks. MMLU evaluates existing attack/control families; its Caesar-cipher exclusion does not remove that method from earlier comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces a separate accuracy-evaluation protocol: 570 MMLU questions sampled as 10 per subject, zero-shot prompting, temperature zero, a 100-token limit, and GPT-4.1 answer extraction. Caesar-cipher results are excluded because shifting answer letters can confound grading. Existing harmfulness protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new MMLU analysis tests whether attacks degrade general capabilities by comparing tuned models with untuned controls, exposing model-dependent degradation. Existing poisoning-rate, learning-rate, epoch, language, and benign-dataset analyses are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: New Figure 5 reports 95% Wilson binomial confidence intervals for MMLU accuracy. Existing cluster-robust Wald intervals and rank-confidence procedures remain unchanged; no additional training runs or seeds are reported.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds a distinct set of capability results: GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, and GPT-4o mini generally retain MMLU performance under jailbreak-tuning, while GPT-4.1 mini degrades after fine-tuning. Original harmfulness figures and numerical entries in Tables 2–4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The conceptual threat model and attack definitions are unchanged. Neither version supplies a formal theoretical development that is revised in v2; the new evaluation statistics introduce no theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about safeguard removal, attack severity, and preserved capabilities. Adding 'with safeguards destroyed' to the abstract reiterates v1's existing claim of entirely removing safeguards; MMLU adds support rather than redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 interprets MMLU results as evidence of generally preserved capabilities while acknowledging GPT-4.1 mini degradation and possible need for optimization. Section 7 newly clarifies that benign MMLU accuracy is only a proxy and does not directly establish harmful-task capabilities.

D1.justification: New Appendix F supplies the complete MMLU task and extraction prompts, sampling description, generation settings, dated judge model identifier, and Caesar-cipher exclusion rationale. Existing training-resource disclosures and code/data access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hendrycks et al. (2021), Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding, to support the MMLU evaluation. The remaining cited literature and positioning relative to earlier attack research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a localized MMLU results paragraph and appendix, updates the limitations discussion, and makes small wording and cross-reference edits. Tom Tseng is added as an author with corresponding contribution and acknowledgment changes; the overall narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: v2 adds MMLU Figure 5 and two evaluation-prompt boxes. Existing figures retain their graphics, while later figures are renumbered and several appendix figures and tables are repositioned; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v1's capability-preservation narrative lacked an independent benign-capability evaluation. v2 adds a documented MMLU check with confidence intervals, reports the GPT-4.1 mini exception, and explicitly limits what benign accuracy establishes. This strengthens empirical support and qualification, but the evidence remains a proxy covering only four models and does not resolve harmful-task competence.
